quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left part of the lane, next to the centerline.
The right part of the lane, next to the curb.
It depends on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Choose the position that gives you the best visibility and the most space around you. Change your position as traffic changes.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet?

options.text: Motorcycle riders with less than two years of experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle riders under 18.
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, all riders and passengers under 18 must wear helmets. All riders should wear helmets, even if not required by law.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: In bright daylight.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in bright daylight. Wear bright colors and reflective materials while riding, even during the day.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: When passing another vehicle on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for the area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If you lock your rear brake on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire locks on a good road surface, keep it locked until you stop. The motorcycle will stay under control if it is upright and going straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: How should you position your body on the motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your elbows should be slightly bent when you hold the handgrips.

questions.question: Who must wear eye protection?

options.text: Only riders with less than two years of experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders.
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, all motorcycle riders must wear eye protection such as glasses, goggles, a face shield, or a windshield. A face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be positioned in a group?
questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: In a group, less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Park at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
Park without any wheel or fender touching the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
questions.explanation: A parked motorcycle should be at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb. At least one wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride on the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of the lane is safest when passing parked cars. This helps you avoid dangers like car doors opening, people stepping out between cars, and vehicles pulling out. Always be ready to change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake on a motorcycle is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to cross ahead of a train.

questions.question: A helmet provides the most protection if it is all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A helmet offers the best protection when it meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fits snugly all around your head, and has no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. When you see one, you must stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, and then go only when it is safe.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Slow down, let the dog get close, then speed away.
Stop and wait for the dog to leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog get close, then speed away.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog is chasing you, slow down and shift down. Let the dog get close, then accelerate quickly away from it.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do both actions at the same time.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to swerve and brake to avoid a hazard, do them separately. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake. Do not do both at the same time.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: To stay safe when riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Be flexible about your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down to watch the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding through a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: The center of a lane has an oily strip. What does this strip do?

options.text: Should be avoided at all times
Usually gives good traction, except when it is raining
Should only be used if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually gives good traction, except when it is raining
questions.explanation: The oily strip usually provides enough traction for safe riding, except in rain. The strip is about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers
You have limited escape route options

questions.correctAnswerText: You have limited escape route options
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time to react to other drivers and room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: When carrying a load, where should it be secured?
questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Loads should be secured low to keep the motorcycle balanced.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane
Ride in the center portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed on the left. Riding on the right side can be dangerous because it may cause the passing driver to re-enter your lane too quickly.
